question: Who can investigate an official-language complaint involving a Northwest Territories government department?
generated_answer:
The Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for the Northwest Territories can investigate complaints involving government departments. 

The Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for the Northwest Territories is responsible for ensuring that the rights of the public to communicate with and receive services from the government in either of the two official languages (English and French) are respected. If a complaint is made regarding a government department's failure to provide services in an official language, the Office of the Commissioner can investigate the matter. 

The Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for the Northwest Territories is an independent office that reports to the Legislative Assembly. It has the authority to investigate complaints, conduct audits, and make recommendations to the government to improve the delivery of official languages services. 

If you have a complaint about a government department's failure to provide services in an official language, you can contact the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for the Northwest Territories to file a complaint. The Office will then investigate the matter and work with the department to resolve the issue. 

It's important to note that the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for the Northwest Territories can only investigate complaints involving government departments. If you have a complaint about a private business or organization, you would need to contact a different office or agency, such as the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for Canada or the Human Rights Commission of the Northwest Territories. 

In summary, the Office of the Commissioner of Official Languages for the Northwest Territories is the appropriate office to investigate an official-language complaint involving a Northwest Territories government department.
